caseStudies.title: What Happens When AI Actually Works
caseStudies.lede: Three recent projects. Anonymized and composited. No strategy decks.
caseStudies.disclaimer: Composite, anonymized — illustrative patterns from real engagements, not specific client outcomes.

studies.title: Automated Client Response System
studies.problem: Team spent a large share of the day answering repetitive client queries across email and WhatsApp. Response times stretched across the working day. Clients complained about slow turnaround.
studies.built2: Built an n8n workflow that routes incoming queries, drafts context-aware responses using AI, and sends them through approved channels. Human reviews only edge cases.
worked: Mapped 14 repetitive query categories across email and WhatsApp
Drafted 6 reusable response templates with human-review escalation rules
Handed off a runbook plus a 2-person training session for the ops team

studies.title: Frictionless Service Purchase Flow
studies.problem: Buyers abandoned checkout because intake forms duplicated sales calls. Conversion stalled under 4%.
studies.built2: Replaced the static intake with a conversational qualifier that captured the same fields, surfaced pricing, and booked a discovery call only when intent was real.
worked: Drafted 9 qualifying questions aligned to existing discovery framework
Wired Stripe checkout + Google Calendar booking behind a single flow
Cut form completion time from 11 to 3 minutes; conversions rose 3.2×

studies.title: Automated Meeting-to-Action Pipeline
studies.problem: Every client meeting produced 40+ minutes of notes nobody read. Action items surfaced days later in standup, often misattributed.
studies.built2: Built a recording-to-action pipeline: transcript → summary → tasks → CRM. Each step had a human approval gate.
worked: Integrated 3 video platforms with a single transcript service
Designed approval gates so the team could correct attribution before sync
Action items now reach CRM within 4 hours of meeting end

whatThisIsNot.title: What this is NOT for
whatThisIsNot.lede: I'd rather lose a sale than take on work I can't deliver. If these describe you, there are better options.

items.title: Not for enterprise transformation programs
items.body: I work with founders, operators, and small teams — not large organizations running the 2023 playbook with better tools. That's the dabbling trap. If you need a vendor to manage your AI rollout across 500 employees, other consultants are better suited.

items.title: Not for leaders still evaluating whether AI matters
items.body: If you're still forming committees to study AI, start elsewhere. I work with people who are ready to execute — not to write reports.

items.title: Not for people who want AI to do the work for them

aboutMe.title: Who Is Alex Myers?
aboutMe.lede: The questions that keep leaders up at 2 AM aren't about which API to use. They're about whether they'll still matter five years from now. That's not a technology problem. I speak two languages: organizational architecture and human experience. The space between them is where real transformation lives.
paragraphs: Clarity isn't about knowing everything. It's about knowing what actually matters to you. When you fix your mental model, the overwhelm dissolves. You stop reacting to noise and start making decisions from genuine conviction.

My work draws on systems thinking, group dynamics, and a knack for asking the questions nobody else will. I tell you what I actually think, not what you want to hear. That's the foundation of solutions that stick.

forks.label: For the Executive:
forks.body: The edge you're standing at isn't just technological. It's structural, cultural, and deeply human. I help you see the whole field, not just the tools — so your organization moves with intention, not anxiety.

forks.label: For the Individual:
forks.body: If you're building your own AI-powered service, you don't need another vendor. You need a teacher. I work with founders and operators who want to leave the engagement with their own capability, not their own dependency.

mentoring.lede: Most "training" teaches tools. This is different. Whether you're a seasoned executive or early in your career, the real barrier isn't technical—it's the story you're telling yourself about what's coming. I help you rewrite that story, one conversation at a time.
